verses.verse:
बहुत्वाल्पत्वनिर्वाहपुर्वकम् षड्जम् न्यसेत्।
कालमानानुसारेण स्वारावृत्तिम् सृजेत् क्वचित्।१३७।
verses.text: Observing which notes are frequent and which sparing, one should make the nyāsa on Ṣaḍja; and now and then, according to the measure of time, one may create repetition of notes.

commentary.text: That is, whatever note the nyāsa is on, sometimes while making the nyāsa a problem arises when the notes come to more than the regular mātrās of the tāla, or when the number of notes falls short of the tāla's mātrās. To solve that problem the number of notes has to be reduced or increased. Then, according to the śāstra, one should increase the count of whichever note has more importance in the rāga, and reduce the count of the note whose importance is less. Besides this, another way is to join a note of alpatva (sparing use) with a neighbouring note and put both in double speed within one mātrā, or to give a pause of one mātrā on a note of bahutva (frequent use). Doing this makes it easy to weigh the rāga into the tāla. This method has been used in the following gat.

commentary.text: The gat above has also been composed by the method given earlier. While composing, the nyāsa was kept in mind from the first mātrā to the sixteenth, but in use, for the sake of beauty, it was begun from the twelfth mātrā itself and one āvartan (cycle) was taken to run up to the eleventh mātrā. In the same way gats can be made and played by the method given above in many tālas, such as Jhaptāl. Now, after a gat has been composed, if a poem of the same number of mātrās is fitted into that gat, it can become a song and a subject for singing. Some people do just this. It makes it even easier for them to remember the gat. The method by which these should be made pleasing to the ear is described in the next śloka.
